results.summary: This project is a ring-oscillator-based temperature sensor implemented in Verilog. It uses counters to count ring-oscillator cycles within a clock period and sends the result over UART. The design includes internal and external clock inputs, oscillator selection and enable signals, and a reset. It is intended to characterize the temperature versus frequency relationship.

results.summary: This is a framebuffer-less VGA ray-casting game demo implemented in Verilog. It renders a realtime 3D-like view of a hard-coded 16x16 map with textures and flat-colored floor/ceiling, inspired by Wolf3D. A host controller sets the point of view via SPI, and SPI2 sets ceiling/floor colors. It outputs 640x480 VGA at about 60 Hz from a 25 MHz clock and has a partial silicon test report.

The design is educational and demonstrates basic computer architecture. It is tested by loading programs and observing the output. The documentation is brief but sufficient to understand the overall structure.
results.summary: This is a TTRPG dice roller with a simple I2C peripheral, implemented in Verilog. It supports rolling d4 through d20 using button inputs and can drive a two-digit 7-segment display for multi-digit results. The design includes an I2C slave, a PWM-capable GPIO, and configuration pins for display polarity. Silicon test reports are mixed, with one tester reporting no output and the author reporting all functions working.

results.summary: This is an I2C bit error rate tester implemented in SpinalHDL. It is an I2C peripheral that implements an 8-bit ALU over I2C to allow pattern testing and read back accumulated results. It supports open-drain or push-pull modes and various clocking configurations set at power-on reset. The design is intended to be driven by an RP2040 controller and outputs results to a 7-segment display.

results.summary_before: This design is a digital circuit that implements a restoring array divider using full adders and multiplexers. It is a combinational divider that computes division in hardware. The design is purely combinational and does not require a clock. It is intended for arithmetic operations in digital systems.
results.summary: DJ8 is an 8-bit CPU implemented in Verilog with a parallel Flash/RAM interface. It features an 8 x 8-bit register file, 3-4 cycles per instruction, a 15-bit external address bus, and an 8-bit external data bus. A built-in 256-byte demo ROM provides two demos selected by DIP switches at reset. It can connect to parallel flash or RAM and run at full speed without serialization overhead.
